title: Model Landing Zone & Runtime Qualification Pipeline
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Build an end-to-end landing zone pipeline that accepts third-party open-source model weights, converts them into the Redwood runtime artifact format, performs deterministic and performance validation, and publishes a versioned entry to the public model catalog with a performance profile and pin recommendation. This task covers the lightweight converter service, deterministic unit smoke tests, profiling harness integration, telemetry hooks for comparison against historical baselines, and the publish flow (metadata, signatures, and visible runtime profile).
acceptance_criteria: Landing API accepts weight bundle and returns a canonical artifact ID within 5 minutes for typical 7B-13B open checkpoints.
Conversion produces a runtime-consumable .rwdm artifact with artifact manifest that passes deterministic float32/float16 checksum tolerance tests for representative tensors.

Automated validation suite runs on CI and runtime staging: functional correctness (sample tokens), numerical equivalence within configurable tolerance, and a smoke perf run that records throughput & p50/p95 latency to the profiling store.

Published model catalog entry includes: canonical artifact ID, recommended pinned runtime version, quantization recommendations (if available), sample prompts and outputs, and a performance profile (token/s, p50/p95 latency) for at least two sequence-length buckets.
Rollback path: if published profile fails later regressions or security checks, we can mark the catalog entry deprecated and automatically route new requests to the previous pinned variant.
tasks: Design landing API and artifact manifest schema
Implement conversion worker container + ephemeral staging storage
Add deterministic validation harness (tensor-level comparators + sample-generations)
Integrate profiling harness (batch size sweep, seq length buckets) with console telemetry
Implement catalog publish API (metadata, signatures, policy checks)
Build canary publish flow and automated rollback hooks
Add observability: conversion time, memory, GPU utilization, validation failures
implementation_notes: Conversion will reuse the existing weight-transformation microlibrary but produce a new .rwdm manifest that lists kernel metadata, quantization hints, and deterministic seed mapping. To avoid blocking mainline CI, conversion runs in a containerized worker pool with size-based concurrency caps. Deterministic checks use a tolerance table derived from previous onboarding runs; for early iterations we permit wider tolerances for community checkpoints and log detailed diffs for triage. Profiling uses the staging runtime cluster (runtime-1.22) with a small reserved pool to ensure stable measurements.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: We will defer on-host full quantization for community weights to avoid legal/performance regressions; instead we will publish suggested quantization profiles generated by an offline pass.

Deterministic equivalence is defined as elementwise relative tolerance (rtol) + absolute tolerance (atol) thresholds per tensor shape — not perfect bitwise identity — to accommodate framework export variability.
Initial publish will be opt-in for public catalog; security review must clear before making entries discoverable.
progress_updates: 2025-01-28: Spike complete for conversion container and basic manifest schema. Verified conversion of a benchmark 7B checkpoint to .rwdm in ~4m on a p3.2x instance. - Liam

2025-02-12: Deterministic harness prototype integrated; floating point diffs within rtol=1e-3 for activations on initial example. Noted two transformer layer ops that require alternate kernel ordering; filed follow-up patch. - Aisha

2025-02-21: Profiling harness integrated with staging profiler service; collected initial token/s and p50/p95 for 128/512 seq buckets. Results saved to profiling-store under onboarding/ENG-209587. - Liam

2025-03-04: QA ran the catalog publish flow end-to-end with a dummy model and observed correct metadata & signature generation. Security reviewers requested additional provenance fields (signed dataset manifest) before public discoverability. - Aisha
review_feedback: PM (Jules Matthis): Add clear user-facing guidance in the catalog entry about recommended runtime (e.g., runtime-1.22) and expected cost band.
Design (Nina Park): Add an explicit sample prompt/expected-output snapshot to help customers detect semantic regression when swapping models.
Infra (Diego Ramirez): Ensure the conversion worker is rate-limited and has backpressure to protect ETL storage during heavy community submissions.
test_plan: Unit tests for manifest generation, integration tests for conversion container in CI with mocked storage, deterministic validation test cases from three representative checkpoints (small, medium, large). Profiling test runs will be executed on staging with fixed seeds and documented in the onboarding run artefact. Acceptance smoke runs include: sample generation (3 prompts), end-to-end catalog publish, and a rollback scenario where the artifact is deprecated and traffic flips to prior variant.
deployment_plan: Phase 1: internal-only onboarding runs and manual review (2 weeks). Phase 2: limited public catalog publish behind feature flag for early partners. Phase 3: full public discoverability after security provenance fields are implemented and audit signed off.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Conversion produces artifacts that are numerically divergent leading to customer complaints. Mitigation: conservative tolerances, detailed diff logs, manual triage for high-variance models.
Risk: Large community uploads overload staging storage. Mitigation: size quotas, per-user rate limits, queued worker pool with backpressure and autoscaling caps.
Risk: Security/provenance gaps delay public release. Mitigation: parallel implementation of signed dataset manifest requirement and early engagement with compliance.
next_steps: Finish security provenance fields, widen CI deterministic test corpus with 5 more community checkpoints, implement feature flag for partner-only publish, and schedule a rollout review with PM/Design/Compliance the week of 2025-03-10.
notes_for_followup: Track conversion worker OOM incidents and instrument heap+GPU allocation per conversion job. Add a lightweight UX for auditors to annotate published entries with review notes.
